fact_rationales.F10: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots can be seen in conditions that affect the nervous system, including leukemias and lymphomas. This finding is moderately supportive of diagnoses like Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B2.1), Lymphoblastic Lymphoma (B2.6), and Burkitt Lymphoma (B2.7), which can involve the nervous system.
fact_rationales.F14: An elevated white blood cell count in the cerebrospinal fluid can be seen in various conditions, but in the context of this patient's presentation, it is more suggestive of a leukemia or lymphoma with CNS involvement, such as Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B2.1), Lymphoblastic Lymphoma (B2.6), or Burkitt Lymphoma (B2.7).
fact_rationales.F16: The presence of 98% atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid is highly suggestive of a hematological malignancy, particularly those with a high propensity for CNS involvement such as Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B2.1), Lymphoblastic Lymphoma (B2.6), and Burkitt Lymphoma (B2.7).
fact_rationales.F7: Leukemia cutis is a skin manifestation of leukemia, which is more commonly associated with acute leukemias such as Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B2.1) and Lymphoblastic Lymphoma (B2.6), as well as Burkitt Lymphoma (B2.7).
